# Create an Asana task from a Discord message

**Pattern:** Command intake -> create -> confirm · **Level:** Production · **Trigger:** Webhook (Discord)

## What it does
Parses a '!task name | due:YYYY-MM-DD | notes' message from Discord and creates a matching Asana task, then replies with the task link.

## Why it exists
The cheapest place to capture work is where the conversation happens. This lets anyone file an Asana task straight from Discord — no Asana login, no context switch.

## Main flow
Receive Discord Command -> Parse '!task' -> Name Present? -> Create Asana Task -> Confirm in Discord (empty -> usage hint; failure -> error rail).

## Use it for
- Filing community/team requests into Asana
- Letting non-Asana teammates create tasks via chat
- A quick '!task' intake channel

## You get
- Zero-context-switch task capture
- Optional due date parsed from the command
- A clickable task link posted back

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Discord webhook URL; Asana access token.
Colour key: 🟦 entry · 🟫 app I/O · ⬜ logic · 🟩 output · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
This is event-driven: your Discord bot POSTs the command to the webhook. Sample data is pinned on the trigger, so hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow end to end before attaching a single credential. Right-click → Unpin when you go live.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never bundled in a template. Every node that talks to an external service needs its own connection before the first real run — open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Discord webhook URL**
Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → Copy Webhook URL. Paste it into n8n's Discord Webhook credential.
_Gotcha:_ A webhook URL is bound to one channel. Use a separate webhook/credential per channel you post to.

**Asana access token**
Asana → My Settings → Apps → Manage Developer Apps → Create Personal Access Token. Paste it into n8n's Asana credential.
_Gotcha:_ The token inherits your Asana permissions — it can only read/write projects your own account can see.

Set each credential up once; it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Nothing happens when the event should fire**
Cause: The workflow is still a draft, or its trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate it. The manual test URL is different from the production URL.

**A node shows a red triangle right after import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials note).

**Task is created with no project**
Cause: The workspace/project GIDs still say YOUR_..., or the token can't see that project.
Fix: Set ASANA_WORKSPACE_GID and ASANA_PROJECT_GID; the token must belong to an account that is a member of the project.

**Due date is ignored**
Cause: The command used a format other than YYYY-MM-DD.
Fix: Asana's due_on expects YYYY-MM-DD; the parser only accepts that shape and silently skips anything else.

**Discord posts nothing / returns 400**
Cause: The message content resolved to an empty string, or the webhook URL is wrong.
Fix: Discord rejects empty content. Check the upstream expression produced text, and re-copy the webhook URL.

Still stuck? The **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there.

## Design decisions

Parsing lives in one Code node because command grammars evolve and a single readable function beats five Set/Regex nodes. The due date is only accepted in Asana's own YYYY-MM-DD format, so a malformed date is dropped rather than rejected by the API mid-run. The empty-name guard stops blank tasks — a junk task is worse than none.

## Practice exercises

Already production-shaped — deepen it:

1. Map an @assignee token in the command to an Asana user GID.
2. Route to different projects based on a #tag in the message.
3. Verify a shared-secret header on the webhook before trusting the payload.

## 🛠 Customize me

Target project/workspace are `ASANA_PROJECT_GID` / `ASANA_WORKSPACE_GID` on **Create Asana Task**. Change the `!task` grammar and the `due:YYYY-MM-DD` parsing in **Parse '!task' Command**. Map an `@assignee` token to an Asana user GID to auto-assign.

## 🔐 Security

Add a shared-secret header check before trusting the webhook — anyone who can POST can create tasks. The Asana token needs write access to the target project only. Don't log raw Discord content if messages may be sensitive.
